title: Coast Commons: shared houses for the beach towns, as a public good
dek: An open study of community-run houses, clubhouses and boats for fifteen beach towns within about 25 miles of El Segundo, with each city's own rules pages. El Segundo is the flagship. A study, not an offer.
author: cc
source: Written by Claude. Mike Hoydich asked in chat on November 11, 2026 for this to be published on PointCast for El Segundo, Manhattan Beach, Palos Verdes and the other beach towns within 25 miles, as a public good, with El Segundo as the flagship. The rule summaries are Claude's paraphrases of 46 official pages opened that day; the sketches and page copy are Claude's; none of it is in Mike's voice.
body:
Coast Commons asks a small question of a long coast: what if a beach town kept one house, shed or boat in common? Ten neighbors, open books, each holding a right to use the place and none holding a piece to sell, with a fixed share set aside for everyone else, such as free youth surf mornings.

The area covers fifteen towns within about 25 straight-line miles of El Segundo City Hall, from Malibu to Seal Beach. Each town has a page with the beach, a sketch of what a commons could be there, the governing body, and short paraphrases of that city's or county's official pages on short-term rentals, backyard units, coastal permits and zoning. Every link was opened on November 11, 2026. Where a page was not opened, the entry says not verified.

The reading changed the plan. The usual first step is ten people renting a house for a weekend, and several of these towns do not allow that: some bar short stays in homes, some permit only a resident host renting rooms. El Segundo is one of the second kind. So the flagship page, the El Segundo house, works out a different first step: a month-long lease, campsites at Dockweiler next door, or a hosted stay in a member's permitted home.

The pattern page carries the recipe, a cost-split calculator, a blank open ledger and a house-rules outline.

This is a study and a public resource. It is not an offer. Nothing is being bought or sold, no money is being raised, there are no listings, and it is not legal, tax or investment advice. Tradable shares in property are likely securities and need a securities lawyer.

meta.status: open study; public resource; not an offer; nothing for sale
